bugs: ProjectObserver/TaskObserver/UserObserver implement ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit but read getOriginal() in saved(). Inside a DB::transaction the handler runs after syncOriginal(), so getOriginal() returns the new value and the old team's dashboard is never invalidated. A probe confirmed it: moving a project between teams inside a transaction left the old team showing project_count 1 (app/Observers/ProjectObserver.php:18, TaskObserver.php:19, UserObserver.php:22)

Exchange rates have no failure cooldown. While the API is down, each request queued on the lock calls the API again after the previous one fails, so many concurrent misses can produce many sequential API calls of up to 3s each. That breaks 'only one request may call the API'. A probe confirmed it: 5 requests against a 500 response made 5 HTTP calls (app/Services/ExchangeRates.php:49-66)
completed_at is never set automatically when status becomes done. Clients have to set it themselves, and a task marked done without it never counts as completed in the last 7 days
antipatterns: routes/api.php:7 puts the 'web' middleware group (sessions/CSRF/cookies) on an API route
routes/api.php:8 adds throttle:60,1, which the task didn't ask for
app/Http/Controllers/ExchangeRatesController.php:15 makes the service return a nullable array and the controller turn null into a 503, where a renderable domain exception would be clearer
app/Dashboard/DashboardCache.php:16-26 has docblocks that narrate design rationale
strengths: Cache::flexible([60,300]) with versioned per-team keys gives immediate invalidation without races from recomputes already in flight
Adds a UserObserver, so member_count changes are invalidated too
The Http client is set up well: baseUrl, timeout + connectTimeout, acceptJson, throw(), and the response shape is validated
Lock with block() plus a re-check of the cache after the wait; it's tested elegantly with Sleep::fake and whenFakingSleep
Clear Pest tests: datasets with named cases, describe blocks, and a test that guest access gets JSON 401 with and without an Accept header

bugs: member_count isn't invalidated when users join or leave a team (there's no User observer). A probe showed a new member doesn't appear until the 60s fresh window ends. The requirement only covers projects and tasks, so this is minor
antipatterns: app/Support/FetchExchangeRates.php:15-25 has a large block of private consts; it's a bit ceremonial
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:117 lock-contention test blocks for 4 real seconds; Sleep::fake would avoid that
tests/Feature/DashboardTest.php:77,131 use DB and Cache facades without importing them, relying on the global aliases
app/Support/TeamDashboard.php:63 reads the version key on every request, an extra cache round-trip (acceptable)
strengths: Cache::flexible([60,300]) with a version key bumped by add+increment; invalidation is immediate and race-safe
Observers use ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit and getPrevious(), which stays correct after commit. A probe confirmed the old team is invalidated when a project moves inside a transaction
TaskObserver::saving sets completed_at when a task is done and clears it when reopened
Exchange rates: lock + block, re-check after the lock, a 10s failure cooldown that stops repeat calls during an outage, a 30-day last-known copy, and timeout(3)
The 503 comes from a renderable exception (ExchangeRatesUnavailable::render), so the controller stays a one-liner
Tests cover cooldown, lock contention, malformed responses, travel()-based expiry, moving projects between teams, and per-team isolation

v.rationale: Both suites pass (impl-2 31 tests, impl-1 32), and the two designs are close: flexible caching with versioned keys, FormRequests that uppercase the currency, and lock+block with a cache re-check. The edge-case probes separated them. impl-1 reads getOriginal() inside after-commit observers, so a project or task moved between teams inside a transaction leaves the old team's dashboard stale (confirmed). It also has no failure cooldown, so during an outage every request queued on the lock calls the API again in turn (5 requests made 5 calls), which breaks the 'only one request calls the API' rule. impl-2 uses getPrevious(), which survives after-commit handling (confirmed). Its cooldown held a down API to one call, and it sets completed_at automatically. impl-1's extras are a User observer that covers member_count, a nicer Sleep::fake lock test and more careful Http client config. They don't outweigh its two correctness bugs, and it also adds 'web' middleware to an API route. impl-2 ranks first.
